query: Consider the following context: Phonon scattering by SRO precipitates might be expected to reduce scattering times and, therefore, decrease thermal conductivity. In that context, which material can be used for lattice heat conductivity, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Materials with short-range order (SRO) precipitates can be used for lattice heat conductivity reduction.
generation.material_initial_state: Crystalline material with potential for SRO precipitates
generation.conditions: Low temperature, presence of phonon scattering
generation.mechanism: Phonon scattering by SRO precipitates reducing scattering times
generation.baseline: Thermal conductivity of crystalline material without SRO precipitates
generation.boundary: Temperature range where phonon scattering is dominant
generation.uncertainty: Effect of SRO precipitate size and distribution on thermal conductivity

falsification_experiment.design: Measure thermal conductivity of crystalline material with and without SRO precipitates at varying temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If thermal conductivity does not decrease with introduction of SRO precipitates, hypothesis is falsified
